newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Lower Danish Feb c/a, trade surplus seen.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Lower Danish Feb c/a, trade surplus seen.

text.p: COPENHAGEN, May 9 (reuter) - Eight analysts polled by Reuters in a survey published on Friday forecast on average lower Danish current account and foreign trade surpluses for February.

The panel predicted an average February current account surplus of 1.5 billion crowns, compared with January's 3.8 billion crown surplus, with estimates in the minus one-plus three billion crown range.

It foresaw a seasonally-adjusted foreign trade surplus, excluding ships, at an average 2.1 billion crowns for the same month, with forecasts spanning one-2.8 billion crowns, against January's 2.6 billion crown surplus.

"One of the main reasons we can see a big drop in the current account surplus is because of expected major payments by Denmark to the European Union in February," one of the most pessimistic analysts, who asked to remain anonymous, told Reuters.
The Danish national statistics office is to release the February current account and foreign trade data on Monday May 12 at 0730 gmt.
